paper text.text:
Suppose $B_1+ab+ad$ is planar. Halin's theorem and
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-cut} give twins $p',q'$
whose neighborhood $X$ contains $a$. Since $X$ meets
each of $\{a,b,c\},\{a,d,e\}$ exactly once, it has
the form $\{a,u,v\}$ with
$u,v\in\operatorname{Int}(B_1)$. The same lemma gives
disjoint $b$--$u$ and $d$--$v$ paths.
Choose $p',q',r,z$ as the four twins.
The set $\operatorname{Int}(B)\cup\{b,c,p,q\}$ is
connected because $c$ has a neighbor in the interior of $B$
and $p,q$ join $b$ to $c$. It lies in a component
outside the new $\Psi_3$, with neighbors at $a,d,e$
through $B$ and at $u$ through the $b$--$u$ path.
Since five neighbors are excluded, this component
has exactly four neighbors and at least
$|\operatorname{Int}(B)|+4$ vertices, contrary to
the choice of $B$. Thus $B_1+ab+ad$ is nonplanar. Since $B_1+ab+ad$ has no $K_5$ minor, choose a
$K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it and apply
Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}. This gives
an allowed minor $B_1'$ with the same three
attachments, connected interior and $B_1'+ab+ad$
nonplanar. Contract the interior of $B$ to $w$
and keep only $\Psi_3$, $B_1'$ and the edges at $w$.
The resulting minor is $\Psi_3\cup B_1'+w$, where
$N(w)=\{a,c,d,e\}$. The graph $\Psi_3+w$ contains $K_{3,3}$ with
parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,w\}$. Thus, in every torus
embedding of $\Psi_3+w$, each component of the complement
of its closed regular neighborhood is a disk by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.
In every such embedding, a facial walk containing
$a,b,d$ has attachment sequence $abad$, up to
cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R7}.
Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore
requires $B_1'+ab+ad$ to be planar, a contradiction.
Hence this minor is nontoroidal, and minimality
gives $B_1'=B_1$ and $G=\Psi_3\cup B_1+w$.

what: Every rotation system of Psi_3 + w with N(w) = {a,c,d,e}. Attachments a, b, c, d, e; twins and w omitted. The claim retains a, b, d, the attachments of B_1.
how to read: For each graph: 'cyclic orders' lists, for every vertex, all cyclic orders of its neighbours, each starting with its alphabetically first neighbour (the other neighbours follow in every possible order, in lexicographic order). Rotation system number i (counting from 0) takes at each vertex the cyclic order whose position is the corresponding digit of i, written in the mixed radix given by the numbers of cyclic orders in the order of 'vertices', the last vertex varying fastest (the order of Python's itertools.product). Facial walks are traced by the rule used throughout the supplement: after the dart u->v comes v->w, where w follows u in the cyclic order at v. The genus is (2 - V + E - F)/2. The attachment sequence of a facial walk lists the attachments it passes through, in walk order, one entry per passage; it is written from its lexicographically least cyclic shift, keeping the direction of the walk, and the faces of a row are sorted. Since many rotation systems give the same row, the distinct rows are listed once under 'distinct rows' and 'rows' gives, for every rotation system in order, the position of its row in that list. 'Up to cyclic shift and reversal' in the claims means the least sequence among all cyclic shifts of the sequence and of its reverse.

graphs.name: Psi_3 + w, N(w) = {a,c,d,e}
graphs.row format: [genus, attachment sequences of the facial walks]

claims.statement: The exterior contains K_{3,3}, so it has no planar rotation; in every genus-one rotation, each facial walk containing a, b, d has attachment sequence abad, up to cyclic shift and reversal (retaining a, b, d).
